paper.title: Pathways Through Public Services for Maltreated Children in Care: A Scoping Review of Studies Using Linked Administrative Data
paper.journal: International Journal of Population Data Science
paper.code_data_availability: No data or code availability statement and no Statistics Denmark (DST) project reference appear in the article. …

sample.universe: Published studies from across the globe that used linked administrative data to examine service pathways and outcomes for maltreated children in care - not a register sample of individuals. The abstract names Wales, England and Denmark only as the sites of 'specifically planned linked routine data work' in the future SERENA project.
sample.unit_of_observation: study (a published study using linked administrative data)
selection_rules: Searched eight databases, identifying 1086 potentially relevant records
Of these, 396 were selected for review
Included 137 studies across the globe that examined contact with services, including health, social care, education, justice, homelessness, and employment before or after children went into care

construction_notes: The article is a one-page International Journal of Population Data Science conference abstract describing a scoping review that is still in progress ('Results will be tabulated and narratively synthesized'; the reported education findings are labelled 'Preliminary findings').

No Danish (or other) administrative register is named, so data.registers is empty: the abstract speaks only of 'linked administrative data' and of planned 'linked routine data work in Wales, England, and Denmark'. Denmark enters as a site of future work and through a co-author's affiliation, not as a data source for the findings reported here.

There is no estimation dataset, no variable construction, no estimator, no equation, no table and no figure; digest.json accordingly lists 0 regressions and 0 figures, so every exhibit id in this extraction is null.

No numeric result of any kind is printed except the search counts (1086 records, 396 selected, 137 included) and the count of eight databases; every claim-level magnitude field is therefore null with an `absent` evidence record.

Only education-sector findings are reported, although the included studies also examined health, social care, justice, homelessness and employment service contact (recorded in outcomes_examined_not_reported on every claim).

claims.statement: Compared with their peers, care-experienced children have poorer educational attainment (preliminary education-sector synthesis of the included studies).

definition.value: Children who went into care (out-of-home care), as identified in the included studies; the contrast group is 'their peers'. The abstract defines neither the care spell, the age at entry, the placement type, nor the composition of the peer group.
Educational attainment as reported in the included education-sector studies; the abstract gives no measure, scale, test, grade or construction, only the word 'poorer'.

estimand.target_population: Care-experienced children in the education-sector studies included in the review, relative to their peers.

population.region: Global - '137 studies across the globe'; the abstract names Wales, England and Denmark only as sites of planned future linked-data work
population.selection: Studies retrieved from a search of eight databases (1086 records identified, 396 selected for review, screened in duplicate, 137 included); within those studies, children who went into care and the comparison groups the studies themselves used
population.description: Children in the education-sector studies included in the review: maltreated children who went into care, set against the comparison group each study used. 137 studies from across the globe were included; the abstract does not say how many are education-sector studies.

identification.source_of_variation: None. There is no exogenous variation: the review restates, in direction only, comparisons made inside the 137 included studies. The abstract names no reform, lottery, discontinuity or shock.

key_assumptions.assumption: Narrative-synthesis comparability: the directions of association reported by the separate included studies are comparable enough to be summarised as one direction for the education sector.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The abstract states only that 'Results will be tabulated and narratively synthesized'; no pooling model, weighting or heterogeneity assessment is described.

key_assumptions.assumption: Comparability of the peer group: the children in care are treated as comparable to 'their peers', and the contrast is reported without any stated adjustment, matching or identifying assumption.

estimator.value: None reported. The finding is a narrative synthesis of the directions of association reported in the included studies; the abstract names no estimator.

source_table.value: 'Findings' section, p. 1, running text. The article contains no table and no figure, and the digest extracted no exhibit for it.

heterogeneity.finding: Placement instability emerged as a risk factor for poor educational outcomes.
Placement with non-kin foster carers emerged as a risk factor for poor educational outcomes.
There were few differences in educational attainment between children in care and maltreated children who were not in care.

ambiguities: The article is a one-page conference abstract reporting a scoping review, not an empirical register study. The 'Findings' statements are the review's own synthesis across its 137 included studies, so this row is a claim the paper REPORTS rather than a coefficient it estimates; a stricter reading of 'claims the paper tests' would leave this paper with no claims at all.
The paper labels these results 'Preliminary findings from the education sector', so the direction may change in the completed review.
No causal edge is written into graph_fragment: the review reports directions of association with no identification strategy, and the schema's edge kinds would overstate it as a tested causal edge.

evidence.how: The abstract prints no point estimate, standard error, confidence interval, p-value, baseline mean or outcome standard deviation for this finding: the whole article is one page of running text with no table and no figure.

estimator.value: None reported. The finding is a narrative synthesis of the directions of association reported in the included studies; the abstract names no estimator.

source_table.value: 'Findings' section, p. 1, running text. The article contains no table and no figure, and the digest extracted no exhibit for it.

heterogeneity.finding: Against the general peer population the review reports poorer educational attainment for care-experienced children, whereas against maltreated children who were not in care it reports few differences.

ambiguities: The article is a one-page conference abstract reporting a scoping review, not an empirical register study. The 'Findings' statements are the review's own synthesis across its 137 included studies, so this row is a claim the paper REPORTS rather than a coefficient it estimates; a stricter reading of 'claims the paper tests' would leave this paper with no claims at all.
The paper labels these results 'Preliminary findings from the education sector', so the direction may change in the completed review.
No causal edge is written into graph_fragment: the review reports directions of association with no identification strategy, and the schema's edge kinds would overstate it as a tested causal edge.
'Few differences' is recorded as sign=null: a reported null difference, not a tested null from an estimated coefficient - no estimate or test is printed.

The finding sentence carries both an ff ligature and a hyphenated line break in the PDF text layer ('few diﬀer-/ences'); the quote is transcribed de-hyphenated and de-ligatured and a clean companion span is given as the second quote.

evidence.how: The abstract prints no point estimate, standard error, confidence interval, p-value, baseline mean or outcome standard deviation for this finding: the whole article is one page of running text with no table and no figure.

No administrative register, register variable or data source is named for this variable; the abstract refers only to 'linked administrative data' and, for planned future work, to 'linked routine data work in Wales, England, and Denmark'.
The abstract states no identification strategy, estimating equation, estimator, control set, fixed effects or identifying assumption for the synthesized findings.
No measurement timing, age range, grade level or follow-up horizon is stated for the education outcomes.
The abstract does not state how many of the 137 included studies, or how many children, lie behind the education-sector findings.
The abstract makes no claim about a domain to which the education findings generalise; the Conclusions speak only about what the review will clarify and inform.

anchor_quote.text: There were few differences in educational attainment between children in care and maltreated children who were not in care.
